note: uspto.gov is reachable this session (the prior covered_by_parent decline was written when the proxy refused the CONNECT). The page's own wording is "United States Patent and Trademark Office" (in the site-wide navigation) and "An Agency of the Department of Commerce". A rename to "United States Patent and Trademark Office" would make the check pass.

note: The House's own page for exactly this collective was read: www.house.gov/the-house-explained/officers-and-organizations (2,477 readable chars), whose heading is "Officers and Organizations of the House". It does not label "House Administrative Offices" -- but it does label two of this node's children in content, "Clerk of the House" and "Chief Administrative Officer", so it is the right page and the curated name is what blocks it. A rename to the House's own "Officers and Organizations of the House" would let this node earn a source and would put its eight child posts on a page that already names two of them.

note: Tested rather than assumed: www.house.gov/committees was read (873 readable chars) and its heading is the bare word "Committees"; nothing on it labels "House Committees", and www.house.gov/ (38,566 chars) does not either. The House does not name an organisational unit of this kind -- the page is an index of the committees themselves. A rename is no help, because "Committees" alone is a single generic token the verifier's own uncheckable floor refuses. Worth passing on: that same page labels 11 of this node's 21 children under the committee fold ("Armed Services", "Energy and Commerce", "Financial Services", "Foreign Affairs", "Homeland Security", "Natural Resources", "Science, Space, and Technology", "Small Business", "Transportation and Infrastructure", "Veterans' Affairs", "Ways and Means"), so it is a strong parent_listing candidate for those committee nodes even though it can never confirm this one.

Tested rather than assumed: www.house.gov/leadership was read (1,913 readable chars) and its heading is the bare word "Leadership"; the page names post-holders ("Speaker of the House", "Majority Leader", "Majority Whip", "Democratic Caucus Vice Chair" all matched as content labels) but never a unit called "House Leadership". The House does not name a body of this kind, and the page's own wording, "Leadership", is a single generic token the verifier would refuse, so no rename rescues it either. The page is still the right check for this node's position children, four of which it already labels.

The graph's own description says "Structure shown is representative" -- this is one template for 435 real member offices, not a body the House names. The verifier refuses the name before any fetch: probe_candidate_pages.py returns uncheckable/curated_count_label for it, the same class as "Individual Senator Offices (100)". Probed anyway against www.house.gov/ (38,566 readable chars) and www.house.gov/representatives (81,704), which lists all 435 members individually; neither carries the curated name, and neither could, since the page lists offices rather than naming a collective.

"VA Medical Centers" is the graph's per-VISN template rollup -- the identical name and description recur under VISN 6 in this same shard -- so no page could ever tell the two nodes apart, and VA names individual facilities ("VA Boston Health Care", read this session at va.gov/boston-health-care/) rather than a VISN-level unit of this name. VA's own VISN page, department.va.gov/integrated-service-networks/ (1,722 readable chars, reached from the old va.gov/health/visns.asp), was probed and labels only "VISN 1" through "VISN 5", never "VA Medical Centers". Flagging for curation, not for nomination: that page opens "The Department of Veterans Affairs comprises 5 Veterans Integrated Service Networks or VISNs" and files Connecticut, DC, Delaware, Maine, Maryland, Massachusetts, New Hampshire, New Jersey and New York under VISN 1 -- the graph carries 18 VISNs and calls VISN 1 "New England", so the parent above this node is stale as well as templated.

The same per-VISN template as the VISN 1 node: identical name, identical description, 26 identical child posts. VA's own department.va.gov/integrated-service-networks/ was read (1,722 readable chars) and labels neither "VA Medical Centers" nor "VISN 6 -- Mid-Atlantic Health Care"; VA now publishes five VISNs numbered 1-5, so there is no VISN 6 on VA's own page to hang this rollup under. VA names its facilities individually (va.gov/durham-health-care/ reads as "VA Durham Health Care"). A curation fix, not a URL: the honest structure is the named medical centers, not a rollup node.

USPS publishes at usps.com (about.usps.com for its organisation pages), which the verifier will not fetch -- the runbook's own example. Two further reasons no nomination could help: the curated name "Districts (multiple)" is refused by the verifier before any fetch (uncheckable_reason_for_node returns name_too_generic), and it is an editorial collective for one Area's districts rather than one named unit, so no page could label it even on a host this project did fetch. Not fetched, per the rule against nominating non-.gov/.mil hosts.
